title: How to think about and talk about money with Ian Dempsey

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间赚钱之外还能赚到更多钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，例如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，从那以后，我也一直支持两届心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励以及我独家的支持套餐，无需额外付费。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个小组智囊团、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南·梅森的零食礼品，以及限时的一对一教练指导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: In today's episode, I am joined by a qualified independent financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我请到了一位合格的独立财务顾问。

sentences.en: It's never too early to start looking at your finances and financial planning.
sentences.zh: 开始审视你的财务状况和财务规划永远不会嫌太早。

sentences.en: It doesn't need to be as scary as you think it might be.
sentences.zh: 它其实没你想的那么可怕。

sentences.en: Stay tuned right to the end to get all of Ian's top tips, and I hope you find it useful.
sentences.zh: 请收听到最后，获取伊恩的所有实用小贴士，希望对你有所帮助。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《有抱负的心理学家播客》。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent, and I am a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: When it comes to talking about money and finances, it can sometimes feel a bit like a dirty word or something that we shouldn't do.
sentences.zh: 当谈到金钱和财务时，它有时会让人感觉有点像个不洁的词，或者是不应该做的事情。

sentences.en: And especially when we look at how we've been raised, we can experience something called money trauma.
sentences.zh: 特别是当我们回顾我们的成长经历时，我们可能会经历一种叫做金钱创伤的东西。

sentences.en: And this is the case that we often find when we're working with clients as well,
sentences.zh: 我们在与客户合作时也经常会发现这种情况，

sentences.en: who might have been raised in chaotic situations where there wasn't enough money or where it was their job to budget and make sure there was enough money to go around.
sentences.zh: 他们可能在混乱的环境中长大，那里没有足够的钱，或者他们的工作就是做预算，确保有足够的钱来维持生活。

sentences.en: Of course, in psychology and mental health, often the relevant experience roles might well be lower paid than might be ideal.
sentences.zh: 当然，在心理学和心理健康领域，相关的经验职位薪酬往往可能低于理想水平。

sentences.en: And so it can feel like there's not enough money to go around and there's not enough money to even consider our financial planning and our options.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们会觉得没有足够的钱来维持生计，甚至没有钱去考虑我们的财务规划和各种选择。

sentences.en: Today, I'm joined by a qualified independent financial advisor, and we're going to talk all things money specifically for this audience of aspiring psychologists and mental health.
sentences.zh: 今天，我邀请了一位合格的独立财务顾问，我们将专门针对有抱负的心理学家和心理健康领域的听众，探讨所有与金钱相关的话题。

sentences.en: If you're watching on YouTube and you find it useful, I'd love it if you'd drop us your feedback or questions in the comments.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在YouTube上观看并且觉得有用，我希望你能在评论区给我们留下反馈或问题。

sentences.en: Please do also like and subscribe to the channel.
sentences.zh: 请同时点赞并订阅该频道。

sentences.en: And if you're listening on podcast and it's on Spotify or Apple podcast,
sentences.zh: 如果你在Spotify或Apple Podcast上收听播客，

sentences.en: please do rate and review because it helps us to bring this podcast to more people that might find it useful.
sentences.zh: 请务必评分和评论，因为这有助于我们将这个播客带给更多觉得它有用的人。

sentences.en: It was an absolute pleasure speaking with Ian, and I hope you find it a useful listen as well.
sentences.zh: 与伊恩交谈绝对是一件令人愉快的事，我希望你也会觉得这是一次有用的收听体验。

sentences.en: I will catch up with you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 我们节目另一端见。

sentences.en: Hi, I just want to welcome along our guest for today, Ian Dempsey.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我只想欢迎我们今天的嘉宾伊恩·登普西。

sentences.en: Ian is an independent financial advisor, the money man.
sentences.zh: 伊恩是一名独立财务顾问，也就是我们的理财达人。

sentences.en: Welcome, Ian.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，伊恩。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being here.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你能来到这里。

sentences.en: People who listen regularly to the podcast will not be surprised that I first stumbled over you on LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 经常听这个播客的人对于我最初在领英上偶然发现你这件事应该不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: That is your main hangout, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是你的主要据点，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: I've just, it's just something that's grown exponentially over the last few years and just been a really powerful tool for me to kind of grow a business, leave employment,
sentences.zh: 我只是，它在过去几年里呈指数级增长，对我来说，它一直是一个非常强大的工具，可以用来发展业务、辞去工作、

sentences.en: kind of get out on my own, do it my way.
sentences.zh: 开始独立创业，用我自己的方式去做。

sentences.en: And it's, it's been great.
sentences.zh: 而且它，它真的很棒。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢。

sentences.en: Ditto in a couple of days time, it will be two years since I became fully self-employed.
sentences.zh: 同样的，再过几天，我就完全自主创业满两年了。

sentences.en: So, um, absolutely think that LinkedIn has been a really big part of that for me.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，绝对认为领英对我来说真的是其中非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It's a great platform.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很棒的平台。

sentences.en: Do you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Spookily, it's about the same kind of timeframe for me as well.
sentences.zh: 诡异的是，这对我来说也是差不多的时间范围。

sentences.en: So, I think we must have kind of made that jump around about the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想我们一定是在差不多同一时间做出那个跳跃的。

sentences.en: So, I've had, I've just hit the one year anniversary for where I am now.
sentences.zh: 因此，我刚刚迎来了我目前所在公司的一周年纪念日。

sentences.en: And previously to that, it was a year, so near enough to the day, we're almost kind of top of the jump at the same time.
sentences.zh: 在此之前是一年，所以差不多就在那一天，我们几乎是在同一时间踏上这一飞跃的。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: Well, it's been lovely having you as a diving buddy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有你这样一个潜水伙伴真是太好了。

sentences.en: I hope the water's been warm for you.
sentences.zh: 希望水温对你来说还算温暖。

sentences.en: It's been choppier times, but we're getting there.
sentences.zh: 曾经有过比较波折的时候，但我们正在熬过去。

sentences.en: Okay, so, you know, I wanted to have you on because it feels like actually something I've not spoken about on the podcast at all is money.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道，我想请你来是因为我觉得我真的一点都没有在播客里谈论过金钱这个话题。

sentences.en: It can be a really tricky area to navigate, especially when you don't have so much of it.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个很难驾驭的领域，特别是当你没有那么多钱的时候。

sentences.en: You know, like many of my audience are likely to be working kind of band four NHS, possibly band five, possibly band six.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的许多听众可能在NHS从事第四级（band four）工作，可能是第五级（band five），也可能是第六级（band six）。

sentences.en: And I had a quick look at what that is.
sentences.zh: 我快速查了一下那具体是多少。

sentences.en: So, band four is yearly £25,000 at starting salary with a monthly take-home of £1,600.
sentences.zh: 因此，第四级起薪为每年25,000英镑，每月到手工资为1,600英镑。

sentences.en: Band five is a gross £28,000 a year with a take-home monthly of £1,700.
sentences.zh: 第五级年薪总额为28,000英镑，每月到手1,700英镑。

sentences.en: And band six, if people are working at band six, it's £35,000 a year starting with take-home of £2,000.
sentences.zh: 至于第六级，如果人们在第六级工作，起薪是每年35,000英镑，到手工资为2,000英镑。

sentences.en: But of course, that's, some of that will be student loan, but I think the student loan only kicks in at a certain amount.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这其中，一部分会是学生贷款，但我认为学生贷款只有在达到一定金额时才会开始扣除。

sentences.en: So, band fours won't pay student loan unless they do it as an additional payment.
sentences.zh: 所以第四级的员工不会偿还学生贷款，除非他们将其作为额外还款。

sentences.en: But sometimes it's useful to think about what amount we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 但有时思考我们所谈论的具体金额是很有用的。

sentences.en: And some of these people will be footloose and fancy free.
sentences.zh: 这些人中有些人会无拘无束、自由自在。

sentences.en: Some of them might already have children.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人可能已经有了孩子。

sentences.en: And so, in these difficult times that we navigate, it's tricky to think about what we do with our money and how we do it, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因此，在我们所经历的这些艰难时期，思考我们如何处理我们的金钱以及如何去做是很棘手的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, it's a massive challenge.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: It's a massive challenge for everybody.
sentences.zh: 这对每个人来说都是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: And if you just kind of look at the squeeze that we've all gone through in the last two years, where you've been through a pandemic, you've been through, like, markets crashing,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看我们在过去两年里所经历的经济紧缩，你经历过大流行，经历过诸如市场崩溃之类的事件，

sentences.en: a real squeeze on people's finances.
sentences.zh: 人们的财务状况受到了真正的挤压。

sentences.en: You've had furlough, people losing jobs.
sentences.zh: 你经历过强制休假（furlough），人们失去了工作。

sentences.en: Then we've kind of come out of that, and it's the talk of a recession, inflation going rampant.
sentences.zh: 然后我们走出了困境，紧接着就是关于经济衰退的讨论，通货膨胀猖獗。

sentences.en: It's a real choppy time for people to kind of manage their finances, whether you're managing a household just on your own, whether you're living with your folks,
sentences.zh: 对于人们来说，这是一个真正动荡的时期，无论你是独自管理一个家庭，还是与父母同住，

sentences.en: whether you're trying to raise a family.
sentences.zh: 无论你是在努力抚养一个家庭。

sentences.en: And kind of, it costs a lot of money to do this stuff, and life is getting more and more expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且，做这些事情要花很多钱，生活变得越来越昂贵。

sentences.en: And as you know, a lot of industries, the wages aren't going up at the same kind of level of pay.
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，在很多行业，工资并没有以同等水平上涨。

sentences.en: So, effectively, if your wages aren't going up at that same pace as the rate of inflation, you're almost, well, in real terms, you're losing money year on year,
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，如果你的工资上涨速度赶不上通货膨胀率，你差不多，嗯，按实际价值计算，你每年都在亏钱，

sentences.en: which is a real challenge for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这对很多人来说是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: But there's lots of things that you can do to kind of make the most of your money.
sentences.zh: 但你可以做很多事情来充分利用你的金钱。

sentences.en: And that's kind of part of what we're going to talk about today and hopefully give you some ideas, some tips,
sentences.zh: 这正是我们今天要讨论的一部分，希望能给你一些想法、一些小贴士、

sentences.en: some ways to kind of make that money stretch out a little bit further and just give you a little bit of an insight as to what a financial advisor does, really.
sentences.zh: 一些让这些钱更经花一点的方法，并让你对财务顾问的真正工作有一些了解。

sentences.en: Great, because I know sometimes the temptation when we don't understand something or if it feels confusing is to run away and hide and bury our heads.
sentences.zh: 太好了，因为我知道有时当我们不理解某事或者感到困惑时，诱惑就是逃跑、躲藏并把头埋起来。

sentences.en: I'm guessing you're going to say that's probably not the wisest course of action, Ian.
sentences.zh: 我猜你会说这可能不是最明智的做法，伊恩。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Like money is a really emotive subject, right?
sentences.zh: 就像金钱是一个非常情绪化的主题，对吧？

sentences.en: And if we talk about money, there are a lot of emotions that kind of sit behind that and kind of do what you do, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 如果我们谈论金钱，有很多情绪隐藏在背后，就像你做的那样，玛丽安。

sentences.en: You'll know the kind of thinking, the thought process, the mind, how all that works behind it.
sentences.zh: 你会了解背后的思考、思维过程、大脑以及所有这一切是如何运作的。

sentences.en: But a lot of that is how you manage your money is influenced by your parents.
sentences.zh: 但其中很大一部分在于你如何管理金钱受制于你的父母。

sentences.en: So how your parents manage money, how you were brought up to manage money.
sentences.zh: 所以你的父母如何管理金钱，你是在怎样的教育下学会管理金钱的。

sentences.en: Was it scarce?
sentences.zh: 它是匮乏的吗？

sentences.en: Was it in abundance?
sentences.zh: 它是丰裕的吗？

sentences.en: And that has a big impact on how you look after your finances moving forward.
sentences.zh: 这会对你以后如何照顾自己的财务状况产生重大影响。

sentences.en: But one of the worst things you can do is the old ostrich of sticking your head in the sand whenever there's a challenge, whenever there's an issue or a problem.
sentences.zh: 但你能做的最糟糕的事情之一就是像老鸵鸟一样，每当遇到挑战、每当有事情或问题时就把头埋在沙子里。

sentences.en: And that's really difficult to do because sometimes that stuff's really stressful.
sentences.zh: 而这真的很难做到，因为有时那些事情真的很 stressful（压力山大）。

sentences.en: And I've been there.
sentences.zh: 我也经历过。

sentences.en: I've done it.
sentences.zh: 我也做过。

sentences.en: This isn't me kind of saying, preach, preach, preach.
sentences.zh: 这不是我在说，说教、说教、说教。

sentences.en: It's like these are things that I've done in the past and I've been in debt and buried my head in the sand because there's a lot of shame attached to stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我过去做过的事情，我曾陷入债务并将头埋在沙子里，因为类似的事情伴随着许多羞耻感。

sentences.en: And you think, I shouldn't have a credit card or I shouldn't have this or I shouldn't have a loan.
sentences.zh: 你会想，我不该有信用卡，或者我不该有这个，我不该有贷款。

sentences.en: I shouldn't be behind on payments.
sentences.zh: 我不应该逾期付款。

sentences.en: But sometimes you are.
sentences.zh: 但有时你就是会这样。

sentences.en: And that's the reality of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是现实。

sentences.en: And I think to improve your finances or to get a better handle on it, one of the things that you have to be able to do is be completely honest with yourself.
sentences.zh: 我认为要改善你的财务状况或更好地掌控它，你必须能做到的一件事就是对自己完全诚实。

sentences.en: It's being able to look in the mirror and just be honest with yourself.
sentences.zh: 这就是能够照镜子并对自己诚实。

sentences.en: If you've got a partner involved, be really honest with your partner.
sentences.zh: 如果你有伴侣，对你的伴侣也要非常诚实。

sentences.en: And that can feel really challenging.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让人感觉极具挑战性。

sentences.en: It did for me, like I hid my debts for the best part of three years from my partner, had the conversation, just said, look, this is where we're at.
sentences.zh: 对我来说就是这样，我向伴侣隐瞒了长达近三年的债务，后来进行了交谈，直接说，看，这就是我们的现状。

sentences.en: She was like, well, why didn't you tell me sooner?
sentences.zh: 她当时就说，好吧，你为什么不早点告诉我？

sentences.en: That was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: Why didn't you tell me sooner?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不早点告诉我？

sentences.en: Let's figure out how we get out of it.
sentences.zh: 让我们想办法怎么摆脱它。

sentences.en: And that was it.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And I'd spent three years of stress and worry by not being in control of my finances, granted a few years back.
sentences.zh: 由于无法掌控自己的财务，我度过了三年充满压力和担忧的生活，当然那是几年前的事了。

sentences.en: But it was tough.
sentences.zh: 但那段经历很艰难。

sentences.en: And I think, go back to what you said, burying your head in the sand and just ignoring this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我想，回到你刚才所说的话，把头埋在沙子里并对这些事情视而不见。

sentences.en: It doesn't go away.
sentences.zh: 它不会自己消失。

sentences.en: The problem of whether you've got really expensive kind of outgoings, whether you kind of really need to earn more money, whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 不管你是有非常昂贵的日常开销，还是你真的需要赚更多的钱，不管是什么问题。

sentences.en: But running away from your problems very rarely solves them.
sentences.zh: 但是逃避问题很少能解决问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there's just so many parallels here with mental health, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 这里与心理健康有如此多的相似之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, that we can think that it's going to get better if we just kind of ignore it and it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可能会认为如果我们不去理会它，情况就会变好，但其实并没有。

sentences.en: But of course, mental health can be so impacted upon by finances, can't it?
sentences.zh: 但当然，心理健康会受到财务状况的极大影响，不是吗？

sentences.en: You know, the two are very much interwoven.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这两者是紧密交织在一起的。

sentences.en: And the idea of financial trauma as well, either from growing up, not having enough money or from just the ideas, like you said, that our parents pass down to us.
sentences.zh: 还有财务创伤的概念，无论是由于成长过程中没有足够的钱，还是仅仅源于那些想法，就像你说的，我们的父母传给我们的。

sentences.en: You know, money doesn't grow on trees.
sentences.zh: 你知道，金钱不是从树上长出来的。

sentences.en: You know, you're being frivolous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你太轻率挥霍了。

sentences.en: You don't need to spend that.
sentences.zh: 你不需要花那个钱。

sentences.en: You know, my mum is definitely, I think of her approach to money is, you know, pounds look after the pennies and the pounds look after themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我妈妈绝对是这样，我认为她对待金钱的态度是，照顾好便士，英镑自然会照顾好自己。

sentences.en: And if she was taking me out for lunch and going to a shop, I could have any sandwich I wanted.
sentences.zh: 如果她带我出去吃午饭并去商店，我可以买任何我想要的 三明治。

sentences.en: But if I didn't pick egg, which was the cheapest, I'd be in trouble.
sentences.zh: 但如果我没有选鸡蛋口味的（那是里面最便宜的），我就会有麻烦。

sentences.en: She'd be annoyed.
sentences.zh: 她会生气的。

sentences.en: Like, that's how I grew up with money.
sentences.zh: 这就是我带着对金钱的这种观念长大的方式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite similar.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这挺相似的。

sentences.en: Like, I kind of grew up on both sides of the fence.
sentences.zh: 就像我是在篱笆的两边长大的。

sentences.en: So, like, my dad ran his own business as an IFA.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如我爸爸自己经营一家独立财务顾问公司（IFA）。

sentences.en: And I've ended up doing it.
sentences.zh: 而我最后也做了这个。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道为什么。

sentences.en: My mum on the other side kind of didn't have a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈在另一边，没有什么钱。

sentences.en: So, I've kind of seen both sides of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我两边的情况都见识过了。

sentences.en: And it's a blend of the two in the middle for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是中间两者的结合。

sentences.en: Like, there's times when I could, over the years, I've certainly done it.
sentences.zh: 就像有时我可以，多年来我确实这样做过。

sentences.en: I've just been completely reckless and thought, stuff it'll come back at some point.
sentences.zh: 我曾经完全鲁莽，心想，管它的，反正总有一天钱会回来的。

sentences.en: But it's hard managing that stuff.
sentences.zh: 但管理这些事情很难。

sentences.en: And I think if you look generationally at where your parents or where your grandparents were, there's a few factors that you need to think about when you look at that.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你从代际角度来看你的父母或祖父母所处的时代，当你审视这一点时，有几个因素你需要考虑。

sentences.en: Is, actually, they probably got a lot more bang for their buck in terms of their take-home pay.
sentences.zh: 那就是，实际上，就他们的到手工资而言，他们花的钱可能物超所值得多。

sentences.en: Like, how much could you buy your house for?
sentences.zh: 比如，你以前能用多少钱买下你的房子？

sentences.en: I've had clients that have bought three or four bedroom houses over the years.
sentences.zh: 这些年来，我有过一些客户，他们买过三居室或四居室的房子。
比如，只要1.8万英镑。

sentences.en: And where would you get that now?
sentences.zh: 你现在去哪里找这样的价格？

sentences.en: You just don't get it.
sentences.zh: 根本找不到了。

sentences.en: It's impossible.
sentences.zh: 这不可能。

sentences.en: They get a lot more bang for their buck.
sentences.zh: 他们的钱花得更值了。

sentences.en: Their take-home pay, the whole structure of work was very different.
sentences.zh: 他们的实际收入，整个工作的结构，都非常不一样。

sentences.en: And you've only got to just take a little bit of reflection time and look at yourself and think about how many adverts have you been emailed this morning?
sentences.zh: 你只需要花一点时间反思一下，审视一下自己，想想你今天早上收到了多少广告邮件？

sentences.en: How many have you seen on TV?
sentences.zh: 你在电视上看到了多少？

sentences.en: How many have you seen on social media, on the radio, or wherever?
sentences.zh: 你在社交媒体、广播或其他任何地方看到了多少？

sentences.en: It's thousands and thousands every day that are all designed to suck that money out of your pocket and pay somebody.
sentences.zh: 每天都有成千上万条广告，它们的目的都是为了掏空你的口袋，把钱塞进别人的腰包。

sentences.en: And it's very hard to kind of push back against that because the whole construct of society, marketing,
sentences.zh: 要抵制这种现象非常难，因为整个社会架构、营销手段

sentences.en: and social media is to suck that money out of your pocket and get your spending money.
sentences.zh: 和社交媒体，目的就是把钱从你的口袋里掏出来，让你把钱花掉。

sentences.en: And it's so easy to do because you can get into debt now.
sentences.zh: 而且这太容易做到了，因为现在你可以借贷。

sentences.en: Like, you can get credit for a pair of jeans that cost 50 quid.
sentences.zh: 比如，一条价值50英镑的牛仔裤，你可以分期付款。

sentences.en: You can pay it over three months.
sentences.zh: 你可以分三个月付清。

sentences.en: And that stuff just didn't exist 20, 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 而这些东西在20、30年前根本不存在。

sentences.en: You just couldn't do it.
sentences.zh: 你当时根本做不到。

sentences.en: You had to have a great relationship with your bank manager.
sentences.zh: 你必须和你的银行经理搞好关系。

sentences.en: And maybe you go to church with them on a Sunday and take them in an apple pie to be able to do it.
sentences.zh: 也许你周日会和他们一起去教堂，带去一个苹果派，才能做到这一点。

sentences.en: And that's the stuff that you used to be able to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是以前你能做的事情。

sentences.en: Now it's anybody and everybody can get credit.
sentences.zh: 而现在，任何人、所有人都能获得信贷。

sentences.en: And it's a billion pound industry in the UK.
sentences.zh: 这是英国一个价值数十亿英镑的产业。

sentences.en: And I think that's massively part of the problem because it's just so freely available.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上是问题所在，因为它太容易获得了。

sentences.en: And we don't have to leave the house to spend now, do we?
sentences.zh: 而且我们现在不用出门就能花钱，对吧？

sentences.en: Whereas, you know, before the internet, you absolutely would have had to go out.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，在互联网出现之前，你绝对必须出门。

sentences.en: And I think it's easier to spend money when you're not having to actually handle the paper money as well, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当你实际上不需要经手纸币时，花钱就更容易了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it's huge.
sentences.zh: 哦，这影响太大了。

sentences.en: And that was a big problem for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我也曾是个大问题。

sentences.en: And the one thing that I did to kind of break that cycle was it was the old, like back in old school days before bank accounts and credit cards, it was a brown envelope method.
sentences.zh: 我用来打破这种循环的方法是老方法，就像回到没有银行账户和信用卡的旧时代那样，也就是棕色信封法。

sentences.en: And it was effectively, you'd get your pay and you'd get a lump of cash in your brown envelope.
sentences.zh: 实际上就是，你发工资时，会把一沓现金装进棕色信封里。

sentences.en: And then you'd probably go home, sit down with your partner and say, all right, this is what we've got to pay out this month.
sentences.zh: 然后你可能会回家，和伴侣坐下来，说，好吧，这是我们这个月要支付的开销。

sentences.en: What goes where?
sentences.zh: 哪些钱花在什么地方？

sentences.en: And that would go for your bills.
sentences.zh: 这些用来付账单。

sentences.en: That would go for your shopping.
sentences.zh: 这些用来买日常用品。

sentences.en: That would go for clothes.
sentences.zh: 这些用来买衣服。

sentences.en: That would go for wherever.
sentences.zh: 这些用在其他地方。

sentences.en: And you'd have a series of brown envelopes to do that.
sentences.zh: 你会准备一连串的棕色信封来做这件事。

sentences.en: And even working in financial services in banking up until about six years ago,
sentences.zh: 甚至直到大约六年前，在金融服务和银行业工作期间，

sentences.en: I still struggled to get a hold of my finances because it was of what I'd done previously in life and spent a lot of money on nonsense and just run up debts.
sentences.zh: 我仍然很难掌控自己的财务状况，因为我以前的生活方式，在毫无意义的事情上花了大量金钱，还欠下了债务。

sentences.en: The way that I broke that was exactly that by having cash and physically taking cash out because you're then acutely aware of how much money you're spending on crap,
sentences.zh: 我打破这种状况的方法正是如此，通过使用现金，把现金实实在在地取出来，因为这样你会敏锐地意识到自己在这些废物上花了多少钱，

sentences.en: for want of a better phrase, because it's tap, tap, tap with the card, 10, 15, 20 quid a day can just disappear at a rate of knots.
sentences.zh: 恕我直言，因为刷卡太方便了，轻轻一刷，一天花掉10、15、20英镑转瞬即逝。

sentences.en: And if you're talking about a salary of two, two grand a month, you only need to do that four or five times throughout the month.
sentences.zh: 如果你每月的薪水是两千英镑，你一个月只需要这样来个四五次，

sentences.en: And you've easily spent a few hundred pounds that you probably didn't have.
sentences.zh: 就能轻松花掉几百英镑，而这些钱你可能根本没有。

sentences.en: It's, it's so easy to do.
sentences.zh: 这真的、真的太容易做到了。

sentences.en: So easy to do.
sentences.zh: 太容易做到了。

sentences.en: Such interesting food for thought.
sentences.zh: 真是一个引人深思的话题。

sentences.en: And I think I'm aware there's a bank, a free bank account that allows you to do those pots within it.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，好像有一个银行，一个提供免费银行账户的银行，它允许你在里面设置这些小金库。

sentences.en: Isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是吧？

sentences.en: I think the starling do that, which can be really useful.
sentences.zh: 我觉得Starling银行就有这个功能，这真的很有用。

sentences.en: So you're, you're my face lit up when you said that I talk to every client about that account.
sentences.zh: 所以你，当我提到这个时，你的眼睛都亮了，我向每个客户都推荐那个账户。

sentences.en: I'm pretty good with money now, right?
sentences.zh: 我现在理财挺厉害的，对吧？

sentences.en: So as you'd expect, kind of doing what I do, but we moved all of our bank accounts to starling about three years ago.
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，毕竟我做这行，但我们大约三年前就把所有的银行账户都转到了Starling。

sentences.en: So we've got individual accounts each, we've got a joint account and I've got my business account and it absolutely changed the way I manage money.
sentences.zh: 所以我们每个人都有个人账户，我们有一个联名账户，我还有我的企业账户，这绝对改变了我管理金钱的方式。

sentences.en: And I tell clients exactly the same because part of what I do with the client is to go through a budget planner.
sentences.zh: 我向客户推荐的也完全一样，因为我工作的一部分就是和客户一起过一遍预算规划器。

sentences.en: And I've, I've kind of rejigged that slightly.
sentences.zh: 我稍微重新调整了一下。

sentences.en: So rather than call it a budget planner, I call it a surviving thrive liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我不叫它预算规划器，我叫它“生存与发展清单”。

sentences.en: So split a sheet of A4 paper down the middle on the left hand side, write down what you need to survive.
sentences.zh: 把一张A4纸从中间对折，在左边，写下你生存所需的东西。

sentences.en: So that's your fixed costs, your bills, your, your mortgage, your car insurance, house insurance, food, that kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 也就是你的固定开销、账单、你的按揭贷款、汽车保险、房屋保险、食物，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And on the right hand side, you do your thrive liSt.
sentences.zh: 而在右边，你写下你的发展清单。

sentences.en: So do that off your bank statements.
sentences.zh: 根据你的银行对账单来做这个。

sentences.en: Now, what you can then start to figure out is where your spending is.
sentences.zh: 现在，你就可以开始弄清楚你的钱都花在哪里了。

sentences.en: And the reason starling is so great for that is exactly like you said, you can set up these amazing little sub accounts called spaces.
sentences.zh: Starling之所以在这方面这么棒，正如你所说，你可以建立这些名为“空间”的神奇小子账户。

sentences.en: So we did the exercise, went through everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了这个练习，把所有事情都梳理了一遍。

sentences.en: And we've got a space for kids, haircuts, school uniform when the dog needs a groom, car probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我们为孩子、理发、校服、狗狗需要美容、汽车故障设立了空间。

sentences.en: So if there's any problems with the car, we've got a one called hit the fan fund because there's always some little expenses that just pop up.
sentences.zh: 所以如果汽车有任何问题，我们还有一个叫做“突发状况基金”的空间，因为总会有一些小开销突然冒出来。

sentences.en: We've got kids pocket money.
sentences.zh: 我们有给孩子的零花钱。

sentences.en: We, I was trying to save up for a set of gold clubs, but that's got out the window now.
sentences.zh: 我们，我原本想存钱买一套高尔夫球杆，但这现在已经泡汤了。

sentences.en: So that's disappeared.
sentences.zh: 所以那个取消了。

sentences.en: But what I love is that we worked our expenditure out over the year.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢的是，我们计算了一整年的支出。

sentences.en: So we knew that the MOTs were going to come for the car.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道汽车要做年检了。

sentences.en: So we knew that in, I think it was March, they're going to come through as the cars get a bit older.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道在，我想是三月份，随着车龄增长，这笔费用要来了。

sentences.en: There's probably going to be a little bit more.
sentences.zh: 可能还会多花一点。

sentences.en: So every month, something goes into that space.
sentences.zh: 所以每个月，都会有一些钱存入那个空间。

sentences.en: And you can name the space, whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 你可以给这个空间起任何你想要的名字。

sentences.en: You can put a picture of whatever you want on there as well.
sentences.zh: 你还可以在上面放任何你想要的图片。

sentences.en: So yeah, every time you open your app, you build an engagement.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，每次你打开应用，你都在建立一种互动。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things when you talk about budget planning and managing your finances, a lot of people think it's really restrictive.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当你谈到预算规划和理财时，很多人觉得这非常束缚人。

sentences.en: And it can feel like it if you've never done that before, as in you just go out and tap your card away willy nilly to do whatever you like with it.
sentences.zh: 如果你从没做过，就会有这种感觉，就像你可以随心所欲、毫无节制地随便刷卡做任何你想做的事。

sentences.en: But by having those spaces, it's exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 但有了这些空间，情况恰恰相反。

sentences.en: The first or the second month that had happened, we kind of got to the end of the month,
sentences.zh: 事情发生的第一个月或第二个月，我们到了月末，

sentences.en: looked down at the accounts and panicked because we thought there must have been a direct debit that hasn't come out.
sentences.zh: 低头看了看账户，然后恐慌了，因为我们以为肯定有什么直接借记没有扣除。

sentences.en: There's something gone out that we're not aware about.
sentences.zh: 有什么我们不知道的扣款出去了。

sentences.en: Went back through, looked through the statements.
sentences.zh: 我们回过头去，查看了对账单。

sentences.en: And it was the opposite because we knew everything was covered.
sentences.zh: 结果恰恰相反，因为我们知道一切都在掌控之中。

sentences.en: So what it means moving forward now is when the kids need some school shoes, when the kids need the football fees, it's all there, ready to go.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着从现在开始，当孩子们需要新校鞋、需要交足球费时，钱都在那里，随时可以用。

sentences.en: So you're not having those one-off expenses.
sentences.zh: 这样你就不会有那些突如其来的零星开销了。

sentences.en: And it's like you just said there, Marion, it's so powerful having that functionality built into the accounts.
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才说的，玛丽安，账户里内置这种功能真是太强大了。

sentences.en: That's why I love those accounts and talk to everyone about them.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我喜欢这些账户并向所有人推荐它们。

sentences.en: But it also kind of makes me wonder why that wasn't done much sooner with some of the traditional stuff.
sentences.zh: 但这也让我纳闷，为什么传统机构没有早点推出这样的功能。

sentences.en: Potentially life-changing stuff.
sentences.zh: 这可能会改变生活。

sentences.en: But what we know about humans as well, Ian, is we don't always love change, do we?
sentences.zh: 但伊恩，我们也了解人类，我们并不总是喜欢改变，对吧？

sentences.en: And we can feel a sense of loyalty and kind of traditional.
sentences.zh: 我们会有一种忠诚感和守旧心理。

sentences.en: And I have changed my bank account.
sentences.zh: 而我确实换过我的银行账户。

sentences.en: So I originally was with HSBC until it got to the stage where I thought, they're not even giving me intereSt.
sentences.zh: 我最初用的是汇丰银行，直到有一天我觉得，他们甚至不给我利息。

sentences.en: I'm not having it.
sentences.zh: 我受够了。

sentences.en: I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 我要走。

sentences.en: And so I moved and I went to Halifax.
sentences.zh: 所以我搬走了，去了哈利法克斯银行。

sentences.en: And then originally they had a reward account and it was quite good.
sentences.zh: 最初他们有一个奖励账户，还挺不错的。

sentences.en: And it got worse and worse and worse until they disbanded it at all.
sentences.zh: 但后来它变得越来越差，直到他们彻底取消了它。

sentences.en: I'm not having it.
sentences.zh: 我受够了。

sentences.en: I'm cross.
sentences.zh: 我很生气。

sentences.en: I'm leaving.
sentences.zh: 我要走。

sentences.en: And I moved and I went to Barclays.
sentences.zh: 所以我搬走了，去了巴克莱银行。

sentences.en: And I've been with Barclays ever since.
sentences.zh: 从那以后我一直用巴克莱银行。

sentences.en: And theirs is getting ever slightly less good over time in terms of their rewards.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，他们的奖励机制也变得稍微没那么好了。

sentences.en: But I'm still, as I'm listening to you, thinking, yes, that does sound good.
sentences.zh: 但听你这么说，我心里还是在想，是的，听起来确实不错。

sentences.en: I already do all that in the background with an Excel spreadsheet.
sentences.zh: 我已经在后台用Excel电子表格把这些都做好了。

sentences.en: But actually it's better if it's done for me because then nothing's going to slip through the radar.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如果有人帮我代劳会更好，因为这样就不会有任何遗漏了。

sentences.en: But also I'm thinking, can I be bothered to change it?
sentences.zh: 不过我同时也在想，我懒得去换吗？

sentences.en: You know, because we can be quite lazy creatures of habit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为我们很容易成为墨守成规的懒人。

sentences.en: But that can cost us, can't it?
sentences.zh: 但这可能会让我们付出代价，不是吗？

sentences.en: Oh, like huge.
sentences.zh: 哦，代价太大了。

sentences.en: Like not just on your bank account.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是你的银行账户。

sentences.en: Like if you think about your gas and electricity, your car insurance, those fixed costs every single month.
sentences.zh: 比如你想想你的天然气和电费、你的汽车保险，每个月的这些固定开销。

sentences.en: Companies make a massive amount of money from inertia by us just sitting there and not making changes and not being on top of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 公司通过我们的惰性赚取了巨额利润，因为我们只是坐在那里，不做改变，也不去关注这些事情。

sentences.en: And a bank account is one of the big, big things.
sentences.zh: 而银行账户就是其中最大、最重要的一项。

sentences.en: So there's a bank account switch guarantee in place where if you switch your bank account, everything should be moved from one account to the other.
sentences.zh: 所以现在有一项银行账户切换保证制度，如果你切换银行账户，一切都应该从一个账户转移到另一个账户。

sentences.en: I think it's 14 days.
sentences.zh: 我想是14天。

sentences.en: It used to be 28, certainly when I worked in banking.
sentences.zh: 以前是28天，至少在我刚进银行业的时候是这样。

sentences.en: And it was a little bit fraught at the start because there would be a direct debit missed or something and you get a late payment charge.
sentences.zh: 刚开始时确实有点让人提心吊胆，因为可能会漏掉某笔直接借记或者出现逾期付款费用。

sentences.en: But the bank would always compensate you for that.
sentences.zh: 但银行总是会为此对你进行赔偿。

sentences.en: Now it's just ultra slick.
sentences.zh: 现在这个过程已经超级流畅了。

sentences.en: Like within, when we moved our bank account across the store, I think within a day, we got confirmation from them that all the direct debits were set up.
sentences.zh: 比如，当我们把银行账户转到Starling时，我想在一天之内，我们就收到了他们的确认，所有直接借记都设置好了。

sentences.en: They transferred all of the standing orders across.
sentences.zh: 他们转移了所有的常设指令。

sentences.en: They transferred even your existing PEs or people that you've made a payment to in the past, all there.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至转移了你现有的收款人，或者你过去曾付款过的人，全都转移过去了。

sentences.en: It was absolutely seamless.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是无缝衔接。

sentences.en: But it's one of those things where you think, oh, well, I get the insurance or I get cover for my phone or I get this.
sentences.zh: 但总有人会这样想，哦，好吧，我能拿到保险，或者我的手机有保障，或者我有这个。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: That's good.
sentences.zh: 这挺不错的。

sentences.en: It's some good benefits.
sentences.zh: 有一些好福利。

sentences.en: But why are they offering you those benefits?
sentences.zh: 但他们为什么要提供这些福利给你？

sentences.en: Because you're paying for them.
sentences.zh: 因为你在为它们付钱。

sentences.en: You pay for those benefits.
sentences.zh: 你为这些福利付出了代价。

sentences.en: It's like the money that you go into the bank and you put into your bank account and they lend out at a higher percentage or they do something else with it.
sentences.zh: 就像你走进银行存入银行账户的钱，他们以更高的利率贷出去，或者用它做其他事情。

sentences.en: It's a fractional banking system, it's called.
sentences.zh: 这被称为部分准备金银行业务。

sentences.en: Now, if you move that to an account that works for you, forget about the additional benefits, that works for you and makes you aware of your spending.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你把它转移到一个真正适合你的账户，抛开那些额外的福利不谈，这个账户适合你，并能让你意识到自己的消费。

sentences.en: You can see on screen how much you've spent on Amazon this month.
sentences.zh: 你可以在屏幕上看到这个月你在亚马逊上花了多少钱。

sentences.en: You can see that you've got money for the MOT.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到你有钱做年检。

sentences.en: You've got money for the kids' uniform, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 你有钱买孩子的校服，所有这些费用都有着落。

sentences.en: That is worth a lot more than £10 a month for your phone cover or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 这可比每个月花10英镑买手机保险或诸如此类的东西要值钱得多。

sentences.en: And I can encourage anybody to have a look at that stuff and really get your head into it because it's a game changer.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励任何人去了解一下这些，真正走进去体验一下，因为这会改变游戏规则。

sentences.en: And I don't use that word very lightly, but it's phenomenal once you get a handle on that.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是轻率地使用这个词，一旦你掌控了它，这种体验简直太惊人了。

sentences.en: I guess I was just thinking then, you know, what's the worst that could happen?
sentences.zh: 我刚才在想，你知道的，最坏的结果会是什么？

sentences.en: I could change and if I don't like it, I could move back, couldn't I?
sentences.zh: 我可以换，如果我不喜欢，我还可以搬回去，对吧？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。
百分之百。

sentences.en: I mean, you don't necessarily even need to change lock, stock and barrel.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你甚至不一定非要彻底大换血。

sentences.en: You could just open one of these accounts.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以只开一个这样的账户。

sentences.en: I mean, what I'd encourage anybody that listens to this podcast is certainly in the UK, there will be other equivalents outside of the UK.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我会鼓励所有听这个播客的人去尝试，当然这在英国适用，英国境外也会有其他同类产品。

sentences.en: I think Chase over in the States to do something similar is to just go into Google or YouTube, sorry, and type in Starling Bank Account Demonstration,
sentences.zh: 我觉得Chase在美国那边做类似的事情，就是去Google，或者抱歉，是YouTube上搜索“Starling Bank账户演示”，

sentences.en: Monzo Bank Account Demonstration.
sentences.zh: “Monzo银行账户演示”。

sentences.en: And there's a little video that just explains how it all works and what to do.
sentences.zh: 然后会有一个小视频解释它是如何运作的以及该做什么。

sentences.en: You could just go and set an account up and just get a little feel for it and see how it works first before you make the switch across.
sentences.zh: 在你决定转过去之前，你可以去开个户，亲自体验一下，看看它是怎么运作的。

sentences.en: And if you then decide to switch over, awesome, it's done.
sentences.zh: 如果你决定转过去，太棒了，事情就成了。

sentences.en: You can do it.
sentences.zh: 你可以做到。

sentences.en: You can dip your toe in with the stuff and if you don't like it, like you've said, close the account and go back to where you were and be stuck in your old ways.
sentences.zh: 你可以先浅尝辄止地试一下，如果你不喜欢，就像你说的，关掉账户，回到原来的地方，继续按老路子过日子。

sentences.en: The good thing about my current account, though, is that I have got a bespoke card with a picture of me and my husband on our wedding day in it.
sentences.zh: 不过，我目前的账户好在有一张定制卡，上面印着我和我先生结婚当天的照片。

sentences.en: Like, that's nice.
sentences.zh: 这感觉挺好的。

sentences.en: That's difficult to take out my wallet, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，把卡从钱包里拿出来都觉得不好意思，

sentences.en: Yeah, of course it is.
sentences.zh: 对，当然是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: But I think over time, like, that's most places will do that now.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得随着时间推移，大多数地方以后都会这么做。

sentences.en: Like, I love that when the Barclays stuff came out because there was a guy that I worked with this last time that came in and a picture of his son on it.
sentences.zh: 巴克莱推出这项服务的时候我可太喜欢了，因为我之前共事过的一个小伙子来上班时，卡上就印着他儿子的照片。

sentences.en: And it was so cute.
sentences.zh: 那真是太可爱了。

sentences.en: Like, he got his card out and he loved it.
sentences.zh: 他每次掏出卡来都爱不释手。

sentences.en: Like, his whole face lit up whenever he got that card out of his wallet.
sentences.zh: 每当他从钱包里掏出那张卡时，整张脸都放光了。

sentences.en: I think it was such a great idea by them.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们这个主意真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, I could talk about money all day, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以，我觉得我能聊一整天钱的事。

sentences.en: This is a great topic to be talking about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的讨论话题。

sentences.en: But many of our audience listening today might well be working in public sector.
sentences.zh: 但我们今天听节目的很多观众可能都在公共部门工作。

sentences.en: They might well be working for the NHS.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能在英国国民保健署（NHS）工作。

sentences.en: And often with that, there's a pension that comes as part of it.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的通常是一份养老金。

sentences.en: Is that going to be enough?
sentences.zh: 那够用吗？

sentences.en: Should we be considering having a private pension in addition to that?
sentences.zh: 除了那份养老金，我们是否应该考虑拥有一个私人养老金？

sentences.en: Let's have a little chat about pensions.
sentences.zh: 让我们来聊聊养老金吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Hot topic, especially at the moment,
sentences.zh: 这是一个热门话题，尤其是现在，

sentences.en: especially when you look at what's recently happened with the budget and the Conservative government lifting the cap on how much it can pay in a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 特别是当你看看最近预算案发生的变化，以及保守党政府取消了终身缴费上限。

sentences.en: But I suppose that's more of the top end of the kind of NHS where you've got the bigger consultants kind of stepping away.
sentences.zh: 但我想这更多关乎NHS的高端群体，也就是那些级别较高、准备退居二线的顾问医生。

sentences.en: But if you kind of look at the lifeblood of the kind of health service and the people, like you say, sit in these bands that we talked about at the start, it's a real.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你看看医疗服务的中坚力量，以及那些像你说的、处于我们刚开始讨论的这些薪级档位的人，这真的是一个……

sentences.en: Well, there's no hard and fast answer is probably the simple way to look at it because it depends on a much bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简单的看法就是没有绝对标准和快速的答案，因为这取决于更大的全局。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I'll always talk to clients around is the first question I'll ask is, like, what do they want to get out of the process?
sentences.zh: 我总是跟客户探讨的一个问题，我问的第一个问题就是：他们想从这个过程中得到什么？

sentences.en: Like, what makes the time that we're going to spend together valuable?
sentences.zh: 比如，是什么让我们将要度过的时间变得有价值？

sentences.en: And ask yourself that same question.
sentences.zh: 你也可以问自己同样的问题。

sentences.en: Like, if you're about to go on the exercise of thinking, right, we need to look big picture stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你正准备开始思考：对，我们需要从宏观上去看问题。

sentences.en: Like, what does our retirement look like?
sentences.zh: 比如，我们的退休生活会是什么样的？

sentences.en: Like, what are the next 5, 10 or 15 years?
sentences.zh: 未来5年、10年或15年是怎样的？

sentences.en: There are a series of questions that you can just ask yourself to really uncover what's important to you.
sentences.zh: 有一系列问题你可以问自己，从而真正发掘出对你来说最重要的是什么。

sentences.en: Now, does a pension play a big part in that?
sentences.zh: 那么，养老金在其中扮演了重要角色吗？

sentences.en: And I think certainly the financial services industry over the years, we've put a massive amount of pressure on people to have a pension.
sentences.zh: 我认为多年来金融服务行业确实给人们施加了巨大的压力，要求他们拥有养老金。

sentences.en: And I think they are very tax efficient.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为它们非常具有税收优势。

sentences.en: They're a great way to save for your future.
sentences.zh: 它们是为未来储蓄的好方法。

sentences.en: But they aren't right for everybody because you might have a partner that is a significant level of income.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不适合所有人，因为你的伴侣可能有着相当可观的收入水平。

sentences.en: So you might not need that level of income.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能不需要那种级别的收入。

sentences.en: You might have buy-to-let property.
sentences.zh: 你可能拥有按揭出租房产。

sentences.en: You might be further down the line and decide you want to downsize the property to give you some equity to be able to fund that retirement.
sentences.zh: 你可能在人生更晚的阶段决定把房子买小一点，换取一些资产净值来资助你的退休生活。

sentences.en: So rather than just think about a pension, what I'll encourage anybody to do is to think about ideal scenario, what does your retirement look like?
sentences.zh: 因此，我鼓励任何人不要只想着养老金，而是去思考：在理想情况下，你的退休生活是什么样的？

sentences.en: And I think if you focus on the numbers, it becomes really transactional.
sentences.zh: 如果你只关注数字，就会变得非常功利。

sentences.en: It can feel really boring as well because I don't like talking about the numbers and that can feel strange for a financial advisor, right?
sentences.zh: 而且会让人觉得非常无聊，因为我其实不喜欢谈论数字，这作为财务顾问听起来可能有点奇怪，对吧？

sentences.en: But my focus is on the important stuff.
sentences.zh: 但我的重点是重要的东西。

sentences.en: So it's going to be about what does that retirement look like?
sentences.zh: 所以这要关于退休生活究竟是什么样的。

sentences.en: And we'll even go so far as to think, well, if you want to retire in Spain and go and live out there, why?
sentences.zh: 我们甚至会深入设想，如果你想去西班牙退休并定居在那儿，为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Where?
sentences.zh: 在哪？

sentences.en: Who with?
sentences.zh: 和谁一起？

sentences.en: When do you want to do it?
sentences.zh: 你什么时候想这么做？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: And paint that picture, like almost paint the villa, paint that scenario in your head.
sentences.zh: 去勾勒出那个画面，几乎就像在脑海里画出那栋别墅，画出那个场景。

sentences.en: Like what's it going to look like getting up every morning and going to have breakfast on your terrace, going down to the beach, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 比如每天早上醒来去露台上吃早餐、去海滩散步，所有这些情景会是什么样。

sentences.en: And once you get that emotional engagement and you can really paint that picture, the numbers can almost become secondary to that and just almost fall into place.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了这种情感上的共鸣，并且能够真正勾勒出那个画面，数字就会变得次要，几乎自然而然地水到渠成了。

sentences.en: Because rather than sitting down with your financial advisor once a year and saying, all right, Marianne, you need to be putting £300 a month into your pension every month.
sentences.zh: 因为相比于每年和你的财务顾问坐在一起一次，然后听到：“好了，玛丽安，你每个月得往养老金里存300英镑。”

sentences.en: And you're like, well, where am I going to find that?
sentences.zh: 而你的反应是：“好吧，我从哪儿去弄这笔钱呢？”

sentences.en: It's OK.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: If you want this villa in Spain to happen, we need to make some changes.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要西班牙的那栋别墅，我们就得做出一些改变。

sentences.en: And those changes are going to be this.
sentences.zh: 而这些改变将是这样的。

sentences.en: You will probably find a way to make that happen more than you need to put £300 a month into your pension.
sentences.zh: 比起每个月必须往养老金里存300英镑，你很可能会更有动力去设法实现那个目标。

sentences.en: Ultimately, the result's the same.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，结果是一样的。

sentences.en: And kind of going back to what you're saying, should people have private pensions as well as the NHS one?
sentences.zh: 回到你刚才的话题，人们除了NHS的养老金之外，还应该拥有私人养老金吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think for years the NHS has been an exceptional pension scheme.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，多年来我认为NHS一直是一个非常出色的养老金计划。

sentences.en: I still think it's an exceptional pension scheme compared to whatever else is out there.
sentences.zh: 与市面上的其他方案相比，我依然认为它是一个卓越的养老金计划。

sentences.en: And boils down to it with a simple fact of can you afford to do it?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，最核心的现实问题是：你是否负担得起？

sentences.en: But realistically, can you afford to put more money in your pension whilst balancing out what you need right now, what you're going to need in the next five to 10 years?
sentences.zh: 但现实地讲，在平衡了你眼下的需求以及未来五到十年的需求之后，你是否还能负担得起往养老金里存更多的钱？

sentences.en: Because ultimately, your pension, you can't touch that on your 55 anyway.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，你的养老金在55岁之前是碰不到的。

sentences.en: That will be 57 before you know it.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，年龄就变成57岁了。

sentences.en: It will be 60 much quicker, certainly by the time we get there.
sentences.zh: 等我们到那个时候，肯定会更快变成60岁。

sentences.en: That money's away for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 那笔钱要被锁存很长很长的时间。

sentences.en: That's the million dollar question.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个价值百万的问题所在。

sentences.en: It's like a set of scales, like almost three scales.
sentences.zh: 它就像一组天平，几乎是三组天平。

sentences.en: It's the short, medium and the long term.
sentences.zh: 分为短期、中期和长期。

sentences.en: And the pension is the long term stuff.
sentences.zh: 养老金就是长期的事。

sentences.en: The medium is five years.
sentences.zh: 中期是五年。

sentences.en: The short term is like, what do you need right now if your washing machine blows up?
sentences.zh: 短期就像是，如果你的洗衣机突然坏了，你眼下需要什么？

sentences.en: It's a rebalancing act.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重新平衡的过程。

sentences.en: Like I said, there's no hard and fast answer to it.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，这个问题没有绝对的标准答案。

sentences.en: Yeah, I feel like I wish I'd known you in 2000 and whenever it was, 2006, I think it was.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得我真希望自己在2000年——或者具体哪一年，好像是2006年——就认识你。

sentences.en: So I'd started in a private hospital.
sentences.zh: 当时我刚进一家私立医院工作。

sentences.en: And at that point, they weren't inviting new members of staff to come into the pension scheme until after three months.
sentences.zh: 那时他们不会邀请新员工在入职前三个月内加入养老金计划。

sentences.en: But I think initially I was on a six month fixed term contract.
sentences.zh: 但我想我最初签的是六个月的固定期限合同。

sentences.en: And so when it came up and they invited me to join, I thought, well, there's probably no point because I'll be out before you know it, you know, if I can't get a new job.
sentences.zh: 所以当合同到期、他们邀请我加入时，我想，嗯，大概没什么意义，因为如果我找不到新工作，不知不觉我就会离职了。

sentences.en: But they did renew my contract.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实续签了我的合同。

sentences.en: And actually, I ended up working there for almost two years and I never got around to joining the pension scheme.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我最后在那里工作了将近两年，却一直没抽出时间加入养老金计划。

sentences.en: And still, I think that was probably quite a stupid decision on my part because I didn't have any fixed overheads.
sentences.zh: 到现在我都觉得，当时的我做了一个相当愚蠢的决定，因为我没有任何固定的生活开销。

sentences.en: I was living with my parents.
sentences.zh: 我和父母住在一起。

sentences.en: I was earning a reasonable wage.
sentences.zh: 我拿着一份不错的薪水。

sentences.en: And I still think that was like wasted money for my future.
sentences.zh: 我仍然觉得那是对我的未来而言白白浪费掉的钱。

sentences.en: Should we be talking these decisions through with people?
sentences.zh: 我们是不是应该和专业人士一起商讨这些决策？
百分之百。

sentences.en: If you look at it at a very simple level, like people look at the word pension and think, boring, that's going to be years away before I'm going to,
sentences.zh: 如果你从一个非常基础的层面来看，人们看到“养老金”这个词就会觉得枯燥，觉得离自己还差好多年，

sentences.en: especially if you're in your 20s, right?
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你正处于20多岁的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: And you're at the point where you think, well, I'll do that later.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，嗯，我以后再处理这事。

sentences.en: In 17 years of experience in financial services, the people that retire at 55 are the ones that started it then.
sentences.zh: 根据我17年的金融服务经验，那些在55岁退休的人，都是在那个年纪（20多岁）就开始着手的人。

sentences.en: And you're not talking massive amounts.
sentences.zh: 而且你谈论的也不是巨额资金。

sentences.en: You're not talking huge commitments.
sentences.zh: 不是什么巨大的承诺。

sentences.en: But think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 但你可以这样想。

sentences.en: The minimum requirement for a pension now as a workplace scheme is an 8% contribution.
sentences.zh: 现在作为工作场所计划的养老金最低要求是8%的缴费率。

sentences.en: So you put in 5%, your employer will put in 3%.
sentences.zh: 也就是你出5%，你的雇主出3%。

sentences.en: On top of that, you'll get your tax relief.
sentences.zh: 在此基础之上，你还能获得税收减免。

sentences.en: So if you get, as a basic rate taxpayer, say 20% tax relief, then you're almost doubling your money before anything else happens.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你作为一个基础税率纳税人，比方说能获得20%的税收减免，那么在其他任何事情发生之前，你的钱几乎就翻倍了。

sentences.en: Because you've got your employer contribution and your tax relief.
sentences.zh: 因为你既有了雇主的缴费，又有了税收减免。

sentences.en: So right off the bat, you put in 100 quid, you're effectively getting nearly 200 pound into that pension.
sentences.zh: 所以开局直接就是，你投了100英镑，实际上相当于有将近200英镑进了那个养老金账户。

sentences.en: It's not quite that, but it's there or thereabouts.
sentences.zh: 虽说不完全是这样，但也八九不离十了。

sentences.en: Where else are you going to get that?
sentences.zh: 你还能去哪儿找到这种好事？

sentences.en: Where else are you going to get that?
sentences.zh: 你还能去哪儿找到这种好事？

sentences.en: And if you did that in your 20s, or maybe even you've got kids and you started doing that for them, because you can do a pension for your kids from birth.
sentences.zh: 如果你在20多岁时这么做，或者也许你有了孩子，开始为他们这么做，因为你可以从孩子出生起就为他们设立养老金。

sentences.en: If you did that for them, they're the ones that will continue paying 150 quid a month into the pension for the rest of their life and retire early.
sentences.zh: 如果你为他们这样做了，他们就会在余生里继续往养老金里每月存150英镑，然后提前退休。

sentences.en: Or get to 65 with a whacking great pension rather than have to get, which the vast majority of people do, get to their 40s, hit the panic button.
sentences.zh: 或者到了65岁时拥有一笔巨额养老金，而不是像绝大多数人那样，到了40多岁时才按响恐慌按钮。

sentences.en: And I'm doing the same.
sentences.zh: 我也经历过一样的情况。

sentences.en: Hit the panic button and think I need to start plowing some serious money into this pension or I'm never going to be able to retire.
sentences.zh: 按响恐慌按钮，觉得我需要开始往这个养老金里注入大笔资金，否则我永远别想退休了。

sentences.en: And I was the same as you.
sentences.zh: 我跟你一样。

sentences.en: I just, I didn't, didn't have one.
sentences.zh: 我就是——当时没有办一个。

sentences.en: Like I worked in banking where the pension schemes were really good.
sentences.zh: 就像我在银行业工作时，那里的养老金计划其实非常好。

sentences.en: Wasn't, wasn't even an interest to me at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时甚至对它一点兴趣都没有。

sentences.en: And then had kids young at 23.
sentences.zh: 然后23岁时很早就有了孩子。

sentences.en: It was then, right.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，对啊。

sentences.en: Can I put money into a pension or can I afford to, I guess, kind of pay for stuff for the kids?
sentences.zh: 我是该把钱存进养老金，还是说我负担得起去给孩子们买东西？

sentences.en: But look back and reflect on it.
sentences.zh: 但回过头来反思一下。

sentences.en: There was always money for a coffee.
sentences.zh: 买咖啡的钱总是有的。

sentences.en: There was probably always money for a beer with me mates.
sentences.zh: 和朋友喝一杯啤酒的钱我大概也总是有的。

sentences.en: It's, it's a tough one to balance because you've kind of, you want to enjoy yourself, right?
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个很难平衡的问题，因为你总是想好好享受生活，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not all about money.
sentences.zh: 生活不只是为了钱。

sentences.en: Like your life, your life shouldn't all be about money and focusing on this stuff and thinking that I need X amount to be able to have a great life when I retire.
sentences.zh: 你的生活不应该全都是钱，不应该只盯着这些事情，觉得我必须拥有X数量的资金才能在退休后过上美好的生活。

sentences.en: And if I don't have that, I'm a failure.
sentences.zh: 如果我没有达到那个目标，我就是个失败者。

sentences.en: The vast majority of people get to their forties and then start really putting that foot down and thinking, right, I need to put in 500, 600 pound a month.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人在40多岁时才开始真正发力，心想：对，我每个月得存500、600英镑。

sentences.en: That's vast majority of clients that I deal with do that because they just haven't had that foresight.
sentences.zh: 我打交道的绝大多数客户都是这么做的，因为他们之前缺乏这种长远眼光。

sentences.en: So you're not alone.
sentences.zh: 所以你并不孤单。

sentences.en: It's not too late if you haven't started a pension in your thirties to start one then, even your forties, even your fifties.
sentences.zh: 如果你在30多岁、甚至40多岁、50多岁时还没开始存养老金，现在开始也为时不晚。

sentences.en: But if you can start it in your twenties, get your kids to start theirs in their twenties and make them more aware of it.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能在20多岁时就开始，让你的孩子也在20多岁时开始并提高他们的意识，那就更好了。

sentences.en: And I think what's quite interesting now is we've got generations of people kind of coming through the system and the education system who are of the Instagram generation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得现在很有趣的一点是，我们迎来了成长于体制和教育系统中的一代又一代人，他们是Instagram的一代。

sentences.en: They are of social media.
sentences.zh: 他们属于社交媒体时代。

sentences.en: They're seeing all this amazing content from financial coaches, financial advisors.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了来自理财教练、财务顾问的所有这些精彩内容。

sentences.en: Where's to make money?
sentences.zh: 钱是怎么赚来的？

sentences.en: And they're a lot more aware of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些事情的意识要强得多。

sentences.en: And I think you've got a generation of kids, certainly a lot of them coming up that are much more financially aware than we ever were because it's all there.
sentences.zh: 我想现在有一代孩子——尤其是许多正在成长起来的年轻人——比我们当年的金融意识要强得多，因为这些信息触手可得。

sentences.en: But the other side of that is that it's a lot easier for them to get money and buy things that they don't necessarily need.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，这也意味着他们更容易搞到钱去买那些不一定必需的东西。

sentences.en: It's a real kind of, again, balancing act.
sentences.zh: 这其实真的有点像是在走钢丝。

sentences.en: I wish I'd done it sooner.
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己能早点开始。

sentences.en: I wish I'd been less embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己当初不要那么尴尬。

sentences.en: I was embarrassed about not having enough money.
sentences.zh: 我曾经为自己没有足够的钱而感到尴尬。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have thought I had enough money to talk to a financial advisor when I was on band four, five, six.
sentences.zh: 当我还在拿第四、五、六级工资的时候，我绝不会觉得自己有足够的钱去咨询理财顾问。

sentences.en: But actually, when I look back now, I didn't have a child until 2013 in my early 30s.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，现在回想起来，直到2013年我三十岁出头时我才生了孩子。

sentences.en: I had so much disposable income before I committed to a mortgage and stuff that that was probably my most abundant time in my life.
sentences.zh: 在我要背上房贷之类的事情之前，我有那么多的可支配收入，那可能是我一生中最富裕的时期。

sentences.en: So I went from band four to band six.
sentences.zh: 所以我从第四级升到了第六级。

sentences.en: And I went from, you know, I was only paying about 300 pounds a month at that point.
sentences.zh: 而且你知道的，那时我每个月只需还大约300英镑。

sentences.en: I remember looking in my bank account on the day that I've got my first full month's pay of band six.
sentences.zh: 我记得领到第一笔完整的第六级月薪的那天，我看了看自己的银行账户。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, my God, that is so much money to me.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，天哪，对当时的我和来说这真的是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: But I didn't have kids.
sentences.zh: 但我那时还没有孩子。

sentences.en: And so this would have been a really excellent time for me to think about starting some investments, even though it felt embarrassing and a bit dirty and a bit like shame filled.
sentences.zh: 所以这本该是我考虑开始进行一些投资的绝佳时机，尽管当时感觉很尴尬、有点难堪，甚至带点负罪感。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我懂的。

sentences.en: It's completely normal because there's a real perception in the financial services industry of some of the financial services industry that you need to have a lot of money to sit down,
sentences.zh: 这完全很正常，因为在金融服务行业中确实存在这样一种刻板印象，部分金融服务行业认为你需要拥有大笔资金，才能坐下来

sentences.en: have these conversations with a financial advisor.
sentences.zh: 与理财顾问进行这些对话。

sentences.en: Now,
sentences.zh: 现在呢，

sentences.en: my view on it is I would have a conversation with anybody about financial advice and money doesn't necessarily mean that we're going to become a client and work together because I'm also running a business.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，我愿意与任何人就理财建议进行交流，而这并不一定意味着我们就要成为客户并合作，因为我同时也在经营着一家公司。

sentences.en: There's cost involved for doing that.
sentences.zh: 这样做是有成本的。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that I can't help you make some of those decisions.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我不能帮你做出其中某些决策。

sentences.en: And I think when you look at like the fintech that's out there, some of the apps to kind of get you started, stalling is a great one to kind of manage your money.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为当你看看现有的金融科技时，比如那些帮你起步的应用程序，Stellar就是一个很好的用来管理资金的工具。

sentences.en: You've then got things like Moneybox.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有像Moneybox这样的产品。

sentences.en: You've then got circa 5,000.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有大约5000的额度。

sentences.en: These are entry level ways to get in.
sentences.zh: 这些都是入门级的途径。

sentences.en: Whereas historically, you wouldn't be able to do that.
sentences.zh: 而在过去，你是无法做到这一点的。

sentences.en: Like that stuff didn't exist when you were probably having your kids, when you had all that money.
sentences.zh: 比如在你可能生孩子的时候、在你拥有所有那些钱的时候，这些东西根本不存在。

sentences.en: You just they just weren't there.
sentences.zh: 它们就是不在那里。

sentences.en: Like how would you have done it?
sentences.zh: 不然你还能怎么做呢？

sentences.en: And I think there's a perception of the financial advisor to be in a gray suit driving a drag and not really interested in you as a person unless you've got 200 grand.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们对理财顾问的印象往往是：穿着灰色西装、开着捷豹，除非你有20万，否则根本对你这个个人不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Part of the challenge we've got is the average age of a financial advisor in the industry is 58.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的挑战之一是，行业中理财顾问的平均年龄是58岁。

sentences.en: And those guys are going to be coming out of the industry in the next five, 10 years or so, which leaves a massive gap.
sentences.zh: 而这些人在未来五到十年左右将陆续退出行业，这就留下了一个巨大的真空。

sentences.en: There aren't enough people coming in at the bottom end.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的新鲜血液从底层进入。

sentences.en: I think technology has got a big part to play and that to serve as some of those people that need help.
sentences.zh: 我认为技术在其中扮演着重要角色，可以为那些需要帮助的人提供服务。

sentences.en: But I think a lot of the experience disappears.
sentences.zh: 但我认为大量的经验将会消失。

sentences.en: A lot of the expertise goes.
sentences.zh: 大量的专业知识将会流失。

sentences.en: And the financial advisors that are left will effectively be able to cherry pick their clients.
sentences.zh: 而留下的理财顾问将实际上能够精挑细选他们的客户。

sentences.en: And I think it becomes more challenging for people to get financial advice because as that market shrinks, which it is doing, then you can effectively pick who you're dealing with.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们获取理财建议将变得更具挑战性，因为随着市场萎缩（事实也确实如此），你实际上可以挑选你想打交道的人。

sentences.en: And that price point might be nearly 200,000 pounds.
sentences.zh: 而那个门槛可能接近20万英镑。

sentences.en: So unless you've got 200 grand, you might not be able to have a conversation with an F8.
sentences.zh: 所以，除非你有20万，否则你可能根本无法与理财顾问对话。

sentences.en: Now, that's just my opinion, but I know others in the industry share that as well.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这只是我的个人意见，但我知道行业内的其他人也有同感。

sentences.en: I think there's a big gap.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里有一个巨大的缺口。

sentences.en: There's still time to address it on how people can get that information and have access to it.
sentences.zh: 关于人们如何获得这些信息并进行访问，仍然有时间去解决它。

sentences.en: And a lot of the time, it can feel like information overload.
sentences.zh: 而且很多时候，这会让人感到信息过载。

sentences.en: Like if you're not necessarily financially literate, like you understand how a pension works, you understand how a bank account or an investment or a savings account works,
sentences.zh: 比如如果你不一定具备金融素养，比如你不懂养老金是如何运作的，不懂银行账户、投资或储蓄账户是如何运作的，

sentences.en: then how are you then going to be able to take that to the next level?
sentences.zh: 那么你又该如何将它提升到下一个水平呢？

sentences.en: You'll probably spend a bit of time looking on the internet, doing some research, looking at YouTube.
sentences.zh: 你可能会花一些时间在互联网上寻找、做一些研究、看YouTube。

sentences.en: But how do you separate the wheat from the chaff?
sentences.zh: 但你又该如何去粗取精呢？

sentences.en: What's the good stuff?
sentences.zh: 什么是真正有用的东西？

sentences.en: And what is absolutely nonsense?
sentences.zh: 又有什么完全是无稽之谈？

sentences.en: Because let's be honest, there's a lot of nonsense out there as well.
sentences.zh: 因为说实话，外面也有很多废话。

sentences.en: Like I think we've got a big responsibility as an industry to do more, to help people make a better financial decision.
sentences.zh: 我觉得作为这个行业，我们有很大的责任做得更多，来帮助人们做出更好的财务决策。

sentences.en: That's certainly what I want to do.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我想要去做的。

sentences.en: And you're doing it well.
sentences.zh: 而且你做得很好。

sentences.en: So I feel like I learn a lot from following you on LinkedIn, definitely.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得从关注你的领英中，我确实学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: And that's definitely what people should do, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这绝对是大家应该做的，对吧？

sentences.en: How could they find you on LinkedIn?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么才能在领英上找到你呢？

sentences.en: Just stick my name into LinkedIn, Ian Dempsey.
sentences.zh: 在领英上直接搜我的名字，Ian Dempsey。

sentences.en: I don't have a website.
sentences.zh: 我没有网站。

sentences.en: That'll probably come at some point in the future.
sentences.zh: 那可能在未来的某个时候才会出现。

sentences.en: I just, well, I mean, when you first get going to business, you just need to get the wheels turning firSt.
sentences.zh: 我只是，嗯，我的意思是，当你刚开始创业时，你首先需要让车轮转动起来。

sentences.en: And there's so many decisions to make.
sentences.zh: 而且有太多的决定需要做。

sentences.en: The thing for me was, right, LinkedIn works.
sentences.zh: 对我的事情来说就是，没错，领英管用。

sentences.en: I know it works.
sentences.zh: 我知道它管用。

sentences.en: I spent a lot of time on there.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间在上面。

sentences.en: I'm going to carry on doing what I'm doing on there.
sentences.zh: 我会继续在上面做我一直在做的事情。

sentences.en: It's education and stuff.
sentences.zh: 那是关于教育和诸如此类的内容。

sentences.en: It's helping people make better financial decisions.
sentences.zh: 这是在帮助人们做出更好的财务决策。

sentences.en: That's where I am.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的现状。

sentences.en: LinkedIn just put Ian Dempsey in and this face will come off and you'll be able to see me on there and see what I'm all about.
sentences.zh: 在领英上输入Ian Dempsey，这张脸就会弹出来，你就能在上面看到我，了解我是个什么样的人。

sentences.en: And honestly, I'm not even just saying it.
sentences.zh: 说真的，我可不仅仅是说说而已。

sentences.en: I feel like I've learned a lot.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己学到了很多。

sentences.en: And you pose really thought-provoking questions and ideas that do make me stop and think.
sentences.zh: 你提出了很多真正引人深思的问题和观点，确实让我停下来思考。

sentences.en: And, you know, the idea and even the word wealth, you know, it's safe to say the word wealth and to think about how wealthy you might want to be one day.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这个概念甚至“财富”这个词，你知道的，大方地说出“财富”这个词，去思考你有一天想变得多么富有，

sentences.en: That's okay, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这没什么不对，对吧？

sentences.en: It's safe.
sentences.zh: 这是安全的。

sentences.en: Of course it is.
sentences.zh: 当然是的。

sentences.en: Like, I mean, people kind of dismiss it and say, like, well, I could be dead in two years' time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们往往不屑一顾，说，嗯，我两年后可能就死了。

sentences.en: You might be, but you might live for another 60 years.
sentences.zh: 你可能确实会死，但你也可能会再活60年。

sentences.en: And do you really want to be worrying about whether you can turn the heat in on because you can't afford it?
sentences.zh: 难道你真的想为自己付不起暖气费而担心能不能开暖气吗？

sentences.en: And I think wealth means – it's a word that's very powerful.
sentences.zh: 我认为财富意味着——这是一个非常有力量的词。

sentences.en: It's very emotive and it stirs up emotions in different people.
sentences.zh: 它非常具有感染力，能在不同的人心中激起情绪。

sentences.en: Like, even the people that are listening to this now will have – that word wealth would have instantly painted an image.
sentences.zh: 比如，即使是现在正在听这番话的人——“财富”这个词也会瞬间在他们脑海中勾勒出一幅画面。

sentences.en: It did for me as soon as you mentioned it.
sentences.zh: 你一提到它，我脑海里就浮现出来了。

sentences.en: It paints an image in your head about what wealth looks like.
sentences.zh: 它会在你脑海中勾勒出一幅关于财富长相的画面。

sentences.en: But everybody's wealthy in lots of different ways.
sentences.zh: 但每个人在许多不同的方面都是富有的。

sentences.en: Like, it doesn't necessarily have to be financially.
sentences.zh: 比如，它不一定非要在财务上体现。

sentences.en: It's about finding what's important to you and how you kind of move to get there and building some financial wealth to help you get there is so important.
sentences.zh: 关键在于找到对你而言重要的事情，以及你如何努力去实现它，而建立一些财务财富来帮助你实现目标是如此重要。

sentences.en: And I think education system's got a part to play in that, which is starting to happen, which is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我认为教育系统在其中也有一份责任，目前这正在发生，这太棒了。

sentences.en: It's about education and helping people kind of make better decisions.
sentences.zh: 这关乎教育，也关乎帮助人们做出更好的决策。

sentences.en: I think exactly like you said, you've learned something from the stuff that I put out there.
sentences.zh: 我想正如你所说的那样，你从我发布的内容中学到了一些东西。

sentences.en: There's a lot of jargon out there.
sentences.zh: 外面有很多行话。

sentences.en: There's a lot of kind of smoke and mirrors for a lot of organisations.
sentences.zh: 对许多机构来说，有很多烟雾弹和迷魂阵。

sentences.en: Not intentionally, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想这并非是有意的。

sentences.en: To a certain extent, the regulator's got a part to play in that in terms of simplifying the information that goes out there.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，监管机构在简化发布的信息方面也有一定的责任。

sentences.en: But I also understand that advisors run businesses.
sentences.zh: 但我也理解顾问们在经营企业。

sentences.en: They need to make money.
sentences.zh: 他们需要赚钱。

sentences.en: They need to be able to feed their family.
sentences.zh: 他们需要养家糊口。

sentences.en: So it's a tough one.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个难题。

sentences.en: It's a tough one to balance out.
sentences.zh: 要平衡这一点真的很不容易。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And many of the people listening to the podcast will be working directly with people supporting their mental health.
sentences.zh: 播客的许多听众将直接与支持他人心理健康的人们一起工作。

sentences.en: And when it comes to benefits and, you know, there not being enough money to go around and things being fair or not fair, is Citizens Advice Bureau still a thing?
sentences.zh: 当涉及到福利救济，以及你知道的，没有足够的钱花、事情公不公平的时候，公民咨询局（Citizens Advice Bureau）现在还存在吗？

sentences.en: Is that still somewhere we can direct people to get, you know, reputable advice, Ian?
sentences.zh: 那仍然是我们能够指引人们去获得可靠建议的地方吗，伊恩？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: I think they do a great job.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们做得非常棒。

sentences.en: I guess the challenge is they're a charity.
sentences.zh: 我想面临的挑战是他们是一个慈善机构。

sentences.en: So they're a voluntary organisation.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是一个志愿组织。

sentences.en: They offer debt counselling services.
sentences.zh: 他们提供债务咨询服务。

sentences.en: Trying to get an appointment with them might be a challenge because there are a lot of people struggling at the moment.
sentences.zh: 想要和他们预约可能会是一个挑战，因为现在有很多挣扎求生的人。

sentences.en: But they are there to help.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实在那里提供帮助。

sentences.en: And what you'll find is that there's a really great structured programme that these volunteers go through with Citizens Advice to be able to sit down in front of you and to give you the help and support for money.
sentences.zh: 你会发现，这些志愿者在公民咨询局经历了一套非常棒的结构化培训，能够坐在你面前，为你提供关于金钱的帮助和支持。

sentences.en: And what happens in the vast majority of occasions is these guys are maybe at the tail end of their career or they've worked with in those particular sectors.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数情况下发生的事情是，这些人可能处于职业生涯的晚期，或者他们曾在这些特定领域工作过。

sentences.en: They've got an incredible amount of knowledge that can give you help and support.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有惊人的知识储备，能够为你提供帮助和支持。

sentences.en: So reach out to these people.
sentences.zh: 所以去联系这些人吧。

sentences.en: There's another one, which is Christians Against Poverty.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个机构，叫做“基督徒反贫困组织”（Christians Against Poverty）。

sentences.en: It's a similar thing to Citizens Advice.
sentences.zh: 它和公民咨询局很相似。

sentences.en: You don't necessarily have to have Christian beliefs to be able to reach out for support, but they can certainly help guide you in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 你并不一定需要有基督教信仰才能寻求支持，但他们绝对可以帮助指引你走向正确的方向。

sentences.en: So there's loads and loads of information out there as well.
sentences.zh: 所以外面也有许许多多的信息。

sentences.en: British Gas and some of the banking organisations as well had, I think, started saying recently, you don't need to be one of our customers to call us and talk about, you know,
sentences.zh: 英国天然气公司和一些银行业机构最近也开始表示，你不需要成为我们的客户也可以打电话给我们，聊聊关于

sentences.en: not having enough money or fuel poverty and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的钱或燃料贫困之类的事情。

sentences.en: Is that anything you know about?
sentences.zh: 这是你了解的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是的。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 他们的确这么做。

sentences.en: I think they're starting to kind of take stock of where their responsibility lies and how to help support people through difficult times.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们开始审视自己的责任所在，以及如何在困难时期帮助支持人们。

sentences.en: Because let's be honest, in this country, we're all in it together.
sentences.zh: 因为说实话，在这个国家，我们都在同一条船上。

sentences.en: Like we've all felt the pinch and felt the squeeze over the last couple of years and things have got more expensive.
sentences.zh: 就像在过去几年里，我们所有人都感受到了紧缩和压力，东西变得更贵了。

sentences.en: The shopping costs a lot more.
sentences.zh: 买菜要花更多的钱。

sentences.en: The supermarket shelves are empty sometimes when you go in there.
sentences.zh: 你去超市的时候，货架有时是空的。

sentences.en: That didn't happen 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这在10年前是不会发生的。

sentences.en: It didn't even happen five years ago.
sentences.zh: 甚至在5年前也没有发生过。

sentences.en: But those banks can help.
sentences.zh: 但那些银行可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: And it's go back to like one of the first things we talked about, Marianne, which was burying your head in the sand.
sentences.zh: 这就回到了我们讨论的第一件事，玛丽安，那就是掩耳盗铃、逃避现实。

sentences.en: Go and have those conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 去和那些人谈谈吧。

sentences.en: As difficult as those conversations might feel for you, the people that you sit in front of will have heard that 100 times before.
sentences.zh: 无论这些对话对你来说多么难以启齿，坐在你对面的人以前可能已经听过一百遍了。

sentences.en: Like there wasn't anything within banking when I certainly worked there that shocked me in terms of financials because I'll have heard it all before.
sentences.zh: 当我还在银行工作时，银行里没有任何事情能在财务方面震惊到我，因为我都已经听过了。

sentences.en: And if you've heard it all before, there'll be a route to help.
sentences.zh: 如果你把所有这些都听过了，就会有一条求助的途径。

sentences.en: Like, again, don't bury your head in the sand.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，不要自欺欺人、逃避现实。

sentences.en: If you need help and support, there's help and support out there.
sentences.zh: 如果你需要帮助和支持，外面就有帮助和支持。

sentences.en: Citizens Advice are great.
sentences.zh: 公民咨询局很棒。

sentences.en: Your bank is great.
sentences.zh: 你的银行很棒。

sentences.en: Christians Against Poverty are great.
sentences.zh: 基督徒反贫困组织很棒。

sentences.en: There are other charities out there that can help as well.
sentences.zh: 外面还有其他可以提供帮助的慈善机构。

sentences.en: And I think the conversation around money needs to be a lot more fluid than it needs to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为关于金钱的讨论需要比现在更加顺畅和自然。

sentences.en: Talk to your family.
sentences.zh: 和你的家人谈谈。

sentences.en: Talk to your friends.
sentences.zh: 和你的朋友谈谈。

sentences.en: It's not rude having these conversations.
sentences.zh: 进行这些对话并不是件粗鲁的事。

sentences.en: Like you're not having conversations about how much do you earn and what do you spend your money on.
sentences.zh: 这就像你不是在讨论你赚多少钱、你的钱花在了什么地方。

sentences.en: And it's like, look, John, I'm in a little bit of debt.
sentences.zh: 而是像，“听着，约翰，我陷入了一点债务危机。”

sentences.en: I don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: “我不知道该怎么办。”

sentences.en: Is there anything that you would suggest?
sentences.zh: “你有什么建议吗？”

sentences.en: Then have those conversations.
sentences.zh: 那就去进行那些对话吧。

sentences.en: Like any of your friends or your close friends would be happy to help you.
sentences.zh: 就像你的任何朋友或亲密朋友都会乐意帮你的那样。

sentences.en: That's not necessarily lending your money to dig you out of a hole.
sentences.zh: 这不一定非得是借钱帮你填补漏洞。

sentences.en: That is, well, do you know what, John?
sentences.zh: 那就是，嗯，你知道吗，约翰？

sentences.en: I've been there and done it.
sentences.zh: 我曾经经历过也做过。

sentences.en: I've never talked to anybody else about it.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有和别人谈过这件事。

sentences.en: But this is what I've done in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我过去所做的事。

sentences.en: That conversation needs to be a lot more open than it currently is.
sentences.zh: 这种对话需要比目前更加开放。

sentences.en: Priceless information there, Ian.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，那里有无价的信息。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for taking the time to talk to us about this really important stuff.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间与我们谈论这些非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: People, as I said, should definitely be following you on LinkedIn because I think your advice is golden.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，大家绝对应该在领英上关注你，因为我认为你的建议是金玉良言。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I've enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我很享受。

sentences.en: I've loved coming on.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来参加。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Lovely.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, it's been an absolute pleasure and I'll look forward to, yeah, connecting with you more on LinkedIn in future.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这绝对是一次非常愉快的交流，我期待着，是的，以后在领英上与你有更多的联系。

sentences.en: Awesome.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: See you soon.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: What wonderful advice.
sentences.zh: 多么棒的建议啊。

sentences.en: And I have to say that since recording this episode with Ian, I did try to move my business banking account to Starling, but they've turned me down.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，自从和伊恩录制完这期节目后，我确实试图把我的商业银行账户转移到星光银行，但他们拒绝了我。

sentences.en: Ian, they've turned me down.
sentences.zh: 伊恩，他们拒绝了我。

sentences.en: They said no.
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I will consider my options.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我会考虑我的选择。

sentences.en: But I believe it is easier to get approved for Starling Personal Bank.
sentences.zh: 但我相信获得星光个人银行的批准会更容易一些。

sentences.en: So, I might well try that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我很可能会去尝试一下。

sentences.en: It's never too early to start thinking about financial planning and it's, you know, there's no greater time than now.
sentences.zh: 开始考虑财务规划永远不会太早，你知道的，现在就是最好的时机。

sentences.en: So, I hope you found this really useful and thought-provoking.
sentences.zh: 所以，我希望你觉得这非常有用且引人深思。

sentences.en: I would love any thoughts you've got about this episode.
sentences.zh: 我很想听听你对这期节目的任何想法。

sentences.en: Come and join me on the Aspiring Psychologist Community free Facebook group.
sentences.zh: 快来加入我的“有抱负的心理学家社区”免费脸书群组吧。

sentences.en: And if you've got any ideas for future episodes of the podcast, please do get in contact and let me know.
sentences.zh: 如果你对本播客未来的节目有任何想法，请务必与我联系并让我知道。

sentences.en: If you'd like to leave me an audio testimonial for the podcast or the book or the membership, please check out www.goodthinkingpsychology.co.uk forward slash podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你想为本播客、书籍或会员计划留下音频评价，请查看 www.goodthinkingpsychology.co.uk 顺便斜杠 podcaSt。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: I will look forward to delivering the next episode of this podcast to you from 6am on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我期待着在周一早上6点开始为您带来本播客的下一期节目。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist, be your guide.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，让它成为你的向导。

sentences.en: With this podcast, let's your side to beyond you.
sentences.zh: 通过这个播客，让我们陪伴你超越自我。

sentences.zh: 欢迎收听由玛丽安博士主持的有抱负的心理学家播客。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你能赚取超越用时间换金钱的收入会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，一名临床心理学家，自2019年以来我一直在开发被动和循环收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一些令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.zh: 苏菲·福特的“一对多”项目现在已经开放报名了。

sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将你的专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.zh: 我在2022年亲自完成了该项目，此后也支持了两届心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个小组智囊团、大师班、个性化指导、福特纳姆和梅森美食，以及限时的一对一辅导奖金。

sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。
